title: How to Stop a Smoke Alarm From Chirping
meta: Smoke alarm chirping every 30 to 60 seconds? Replace the battery, check the manufacture date, clear the end-of-life warning, and know when to replace the whole alarm.
summary: A single chirp every 30 to 60 seconds usually means a low battery: replace it with the type printed on the alarm and press TEST. If it keeps chirping with a new battery, or the alarm is 10 years past its manufacture date, replace the whole alarm.
howto_verb: stop a smoke alarm from chirping
causes: Chirps are warnings, not alarms. Low battery is the most common cause. Sealed 10-year alarms chirp at end of life and cannot take a new battery. Hardwired alarms have a backup battery that also chirps when low. Dust, temperature swings and a battery drawer that is not fully closed can cause chirps too.

tools.name: Soft brush or vacuum attachment
tools.note: To clear dust from the vents

materials.name: Replacement batteries (9V or AA, as printed on the alarm)
materials.note: Use the brand or type the alarm label lists

materials.name: Replacement smoke alarm, if over 10 years old
materials.note: Match hardwired with hardwired; check the connector brand

steps.title: Find the chirping alarm
steps.text: Stand under each alarm and wait. The chirp can echo, and interconnected alarms may all sound when one is the source.

steps.title: Check the date
steps.text: Twist the alarm off its base and look on the back for the manufacture date. NFPA says to replace alarms 10 years from that date, and to replace any alarm with no date.

steps.title: Replace the battery
steps.text: Open the battery drawer, install a fresh battery of the listed type, and close the drawer fully. On hardwired alarms, the backup battery is behind a door or on the side; the alarm can stay connected.

steps.title: Reset and test
steps.text: Reinstall the alarm, press and hold TEST until it sounds. Some models need the test button held for several seconds after a battery change to clear the warning.

steps.title: Clean it
steps.text: Gently vacuum the vents. Dust can cause false alarms and chirps.

steps.title: Replace if it still chirps
steps.text: If the chirp continues with a fresh battery, or it is a sealed 10-year alarm giving an end-of-life signal, replace the alarm. For hardwired alarms, turn off the breaker before unplugging the wiring harness, and use a replacement with a matching connector or follow its instructions.

safety: Do not remove a battery to silence a chirp and leave the alarm empty. Replace it the same day.
Never paint over a smoke alarm.
If the alarm is sounding a full alarm, treat it as a real fire until you are sure it is not.
Hardwired alarm replacement involves household wiring; turn off the breaker first. If the wiring is not a simple plug-in harness, call an electrician.
call_pro: You are adding new hardwired or interconnected alarms.
The wiring at the ceiling box is damaged or does not match the new alarm.
Alarms false-alarm repeatedly with no smoke, steam or dust nearby.

faq.q: How often should I replace smoke alarm batteries?
faq.a: USFA advises replacing hardwired alarm backup batteries at least once a year. Follow the manufacturer's instructions for battery-only models.

faq.q: How long do smoke alarms last?
faq.a: Replace them 10 years from the manufacture date printed on the alarm, per NFPA guidance.

faq.q: How often should I test smoke alarms?
Why does it chirp at night?
faq.a: Homes cool off at night, and a weak battery's voltage drops as it gets colder, which can trigger the low-battery chirp.
